meta.title: SLATE research: household waste collection, cleaning supplies and how fast a home uses them

waste.collector: New York City Department of Sanitation (DSNY)
waste.chargeBasis: No separate household charge found: DSNY curbside collection of trash, recycling, compost and bulk items is a City service
waste.chargeNote: Neither the DSNY nor the NYC311 pages read show a household collection fee. The figure is left null rather than asserting how the City funds it.
waste.frequency: Trash two or three times a week depending on address (DSNY district schedule).

extras.note: Home Depot blocks automated reads; this price is from the search index of that listing. DSNY itself says the bins cost about $50 for the most common size.

extras.item: Containers: properties with 1-9 residential units must use only official NYC Bins for trash from June 1, 2026; full enforcement from September 8, 2026. Trash bins come in 45, 35 and 25 gallons; the 35-gallon is recommended for small single-family homes and holds up to 3 kitchen bags. Recycling and compost NYC Bins are optional. Sold at NYC Home Depot stores.
Fine for setting out trash without a lidded bin of 55 gallons or less: first offense $50, second $100, third and later $200
Bulk items and mattresses: no appointment and no fee; out between 6 p.m. and midnight before collection; mattresses and box springs must be sealed in a plastic bag (fines $50/$100/$200).
Owners of one- and two-family homes receiving STAR could claim an NYC Bin reimbursement; the period closed September 8, 2026.

waste.chargeBasis: Solid Resources Fee per single-family or duplex dwelling, shown on the LADWP bill
waste.chargeNote: householdCharge is the rate in force on 2026-10-02. The fee covers weekly trash, recycling and organics collection and bulky-item collection. The page prints the first step as "November 21, 2026", which cannot be right as it precedes July 1, 2026; the ordinance passed in October 2025 and news reports give the rise from $36.32 to $55.95, so 2025-11-21 is recorded. Qualifying low-income customers get 30% off. taxIncluded: a municipal fee; the page shows no tax on it.

waste.collector: City of New Haven Department of Public Works, Refuse Division
waste.chargeBasis: No separate household collection fee found
waste.chargeNote: A City refuse job bulletin places refuse collection in the General Fund. The City site blocks automated reads (Akamai 403), so the figures here come from its pages as indexed by search and are marked unconfirmed.
waste.frequency: Weekly trash and recycling; brown 48-gallon toter for trash, blue 96-gallon toter for recycling; both out before collection and back within 12 hours.

extras.item: Bulk trash appointment: qualifying homeowners get one free a calendar year; extra appointments, and every tenant appointment, cost $50. No cash or money orders.

waste.collector: City of Toronto Solid Waste Management Services
waste.chargeBasis: Annual rate by garbage bin size, on the City utility bill (a daily bin rate times the days in the billing period); the medium bin is the headline figure

binRates.note: Garbage tags $6.81 each, online or at Toronto Canadian Tire stores.

waste.chargeNote: 2026 rates, up 3.75%. The rebate is not universal: it is for seniors or persons living with a disability with household income of $62,000 or less on single-family residential properties. The bag-only rebate ($215.01) exceeds the bag-only fee ($203.50) as printed. Solid waste charges get no early-payment discount. taxIncluded: the fee as charged; no HST is shown on the page (not independently verified).

waste.chargeBasis: Annual flat utility fees for the garbage cart and the green bin cart, by size, on the property tax notice issued in late May
waste.chargeNote: A household pays its garbage cart fee plus its green bin fee; for example 240 L garbage and 240 L green come to $433 a year. householdCharge is null because no one size is standard. The representative single-family total rose 1.6% ($7) for 2026. vancouver.ca and council.vancouver.ca block automated reads (403 and a Cloudflare check), so these figures come from the City pages and the 2025-11-04 council report as indexed by search; unconfirmed.
waste.frequency: Garbage every two weeks; green bin weekly, with a move to every two weeks announced for January 2027.

waste.collector: Each alcaldía's servicio público de limpia, under the city's Agencia de Gestión Integral de Residuos (AGIR)
waste.chargeBasis: Free for homes by law: article 38 of the Ley de Residuos Sólidos del Distrito Federal makes household collection free of charge (as reported; the law text was not read)
waste.chargeNote: Tips (propinas) are customary but not required. Much of the collection workforce are unpaid "voluntarios" who live on tips and the sale of recyclables; one report puts their tips at 200-300 pesos a day in total, which is not a per-household figure. No per-household tip figure is published, so none is given.
waste.frequency: From 2026-01-01 separation is mandatory: organics (green) Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday; recyclables (grey) and non-recyclables (orange) Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday, in separate bags; bulky and special items (mattresses, furniture, electronics, batteries, tyres) Sunday. Unsorted waste is left, not fined.

extras.item: Collection free by law; tips voluntary
Voluntary collectors and their tip income

waste.sourceNote: The CDMX government servers refused connections on 2026-10-02; the schedule is from Infobae reporting AGIR and from the search index of the SEDEMA page.

waste.collector: The borough council; Lambeth is the named example
waste.chargeBasis: Rubbish, recycling and food waste collection come with council tax; garden waste is an optional paid subscription

extras.item: Lambeth garden waste subscription: collection of 2 reusable bags a week, 12 months
Lambeth reusable garden waste bag, bought separately
Lambeth extra garden waste bag collected, per bag per year
Lambeth roll of 10 compostable garden waste bags (collected at no extra cost)
Lambeth administration charge for paying by cheque
Lambeth bulky waste (items that cannot be reused): up to 3 items £36, up to 6 £70, up to 10 £116; reusable items collected free by Emmaus
Camden bulky waste: 1-5 items or up to 20 black bags £25, 6-10 items £50, 11-15 items £75; two free a year for residents over 65 or on 100% Council Tax Support
extras.note: From the search index of the Camden page, not read directly.

waste.chargeNote: Lambeth's own page reads £99 for 12 months; a search snippet gave £94.75 for 2026/27, which the council page supersedes.
waste.frequency: Lambeth kerbside homes: black-bin rubbish every two weeks (borough-wide from 2024-04-15); recycling, food waste, and small electricals and batteries weekly; garden waste weekly for subscribers.

waste.collector: Private permitted operators chosen by the household (Panda, The City Bin Co., Greyhound and others)
waste.chargeBasis: A private contract: a monthly or annual plan with a general-waste weight allowance, or a service charge plus per-lift and per-kg charges

operators.note: Annual prices include one month free for paying upfront. The Flexi plan appears on the signup page with the same figures under both Galway and Dublin.

plans.plan: Family Value (Dublin City Council area, 3-5 persons)
Family First+ (Dublin City Council area, 5+ persons)
Standard, Family, Family Plus (Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown and Fingal)
Pay as you go (annual service charge)
Pay as you go+ (pay by weight)

operators.note: On subscription plans green and brown bin lifts are free with no weight allowance. The page says excess over the monthly allowance is 30c/kg and "General waste is charged at an additional 6 cent per kg". Direct debit is taken between the 28th and the 1st.

Panda quotes prices only after an Eircode is entered, so these come from Money Guide Ireland ('Figures Verified Aug 2026'), a third-party comparison; it lists unlimited free recycling and compost and fortnightly collection. Panda's pay-per-lift rates could not be read from Panda.

levy.name: Waste Recovery Levy (Circular Economy (Waste Recovery Levy) Regulations 2023)
levy.appliesTo: General waste (black bin) and general skip waste, from 2023-09-01; the landfill levy rose to €85 a tonne the same day

waste.chargeNote: householdCharge is null: there is no single Dublin price; the household picks an operator and plan. taxIncluded: advertised consumer prices; the pages do not state VAT separately.
waste.frequency: Fortnightly per bin for Panda (per Money Guide Ireland); The City Bin Co. and Greyhound pages read do not state a frequency.

usage.measure: loads per year, average American family
usage.note: ENERGY STAR: "The average American family washes about 300 loads of laundry each year." Family size not stated.

usage.measure: washing machine uses per year assumed for running costs
usage.note: Energy Saving Trust: "A 7kg washing machine used 220 times a year will cost typically between £25 – £35 a year to run." A planning assumption, not a measured survey average.

usage.measure: dishwasher cycles per year in the DOE test procedure
usage.note: DOE Appendix C1 used 215 cycles a year; Appendix C2 reduced it to 184, matching AHAM DW-1-2020 and falling real use. From the search index of the Federal Register notice, not read directly. One tablet or pod a cycle.

usage.measure: rolls per person per year, 2018 estimate
usage.note: Statista: an American gets through 141 rolls a year, about 12.7 kg; Germany 134, the UK 127. Roll sizes differ, so the weight is the steadier figure. Toilet-paper products and a per-day use figure are already in research-hygiene.json.

usage.measure: municipal solid waste generated per person per day, 2018
usage.note: All MSW, including commercial and institutional, not households only; 1.16 lb went to recycling and 0.42 lb to composting.

usage.measure: waste from households per person, England, 2023
usage.note: Defra statistics as reported (21.7 million tonnes), including what is recycled; from the search index.

usage.measure: household waste managed per person, Ireland, 2020
usage.note: Panda citing the EPA: 372 kg per person in 2020, 39% of it in the black bin (about 145 kg). The EPA gives 379 kg including unmanaged waste.

notes.method: Supply prices were read on 2026-10-02 from the same public endpoints as research-groceries.json and research-hygiene.json: the Wynshop storefrontgateway search API for Price Rite (store 301), The Fresh Grocer (197), Smart & Final (371), SuperValu (5550) and Save-On-Foods (937); Giant Tiger's Shopify catalogue (search/suggest.json and products/<handle>.js); and Chedraui's VTEX catalog search. Those rows have confirmed:true. Tesco blocks automated reads, so its rows are Tesco's own price row on Trolley.co.uk and have confirmed:false. 'price' is always the regular price (wasWholePrice on Wynshop, compare-at on Giant Tiger, ListPrice on Chedraui); a promotional price is in promoPrice with promoNote. Waste figures were read from each city's or operator's own page where it answered; where a page blocked automated reads, the figure is from its search-indexed text or a named secondary source and the entry is confirmed:false.

fieldNotes.sizeQty: ml for liquids (1 US fl oz = 29.5735 ml, 1 US gal = 3785.41 ml); ct for counted items (tablets, pods, rolls, bags, sponges).
fieldNotes.loads: The wash or cycle count printed on the pack where the listing gives it; null otherwise.
fieldNotes.taxIncluded: true for GB, IE and MX shelf prices (VAT/IVA included); false for US and CA shelf prices, which are before sales tax. Cleaning products are not food, so US and Canadian sales taxes generally apply at the till, but no rate is asserted.
fieldNotes.cityId: The SLATE town the store serves. Price Rite of Hamden is the nearest Price Rite to New Haven; Giant Tiger catalogue prices are regional, with Ontario among the listed provinces.

notes.toiletPaper: Toilet paper products are already in research-hygiene.json (17 rows across every chain) and are not repeated here.
notes.marketsCovered: US (Price Rite, The Fresh Grocer, Smart & Final: all eight categories each), CA (Save-On-Foods, Giant Tiger), IE (SuperValu), MX (Chedraui), GB (Tesco via Trolley). Sainsbury's was not read.
notFound: A separate household waste fee in New York City or New Haven: none appears on the city pages.
Panda's own household prices: quoted only per Eircode on its signup page.
A per-household tip figure for Mexico City collectors: none published.
